auth.withMicrosoft: Use the Microsoft 365 account you already sign in to email with. SUPSERV keeps no password of its own.
auth.failed: Sign-in did not complete. Nothing was changed — try again.
auth.noAccountHelp: Only accounts in the SUPSERV directory can sign in. If yours is refused, ask the Gérant to add you.
auth.noRoleTitle: Your account works, but you have no access yet
auth.noRoleBody: You are signed in as {email}. The Gérant decides what each person may do, and has not assigned you a role. Nothing is broken — ask them to open Settings → Users and roles.

profile.title: My profile
profile.subtitle: Settings that follow you, not the company.
profile.interfaceLanguageHelp: This changes what YOU see. It does not change the language of any document or email — those follow the client or supplier they are addressed to.
profile.documentLanguageHelp: Set on each company, not here. A French client receives French paperwork even when you work in English.

filters.stageHint: More than one value allowed — OR inside a field
filters.ownerHint: AND between fields, OR inside one

views.closingThisWeekAsks: Deadline inside 7 days, not won or lost
views.waitingOnSupplierAsks: Asked, no reply, 2 days or more
views.nothingSentYetAsks: Enquiry open, no offer, older than 3 days

search.title: Search
search.prompt: Companies, contacts, items and references. Spelling does not have to be exact.
search.noneBody: Try fewer words, or part of a name. If a company is known here by another spelling, add it as an alias on its page and every future search will find it.
search.notLookedYet: Search looks in four places: records, documents we generated, files we received, and email bodies. Only records exist so far — the other three are not empty, they have not been looked in yet.

company.newSubtitle: Only the legal name and one role are required. The rest can follow.
company.identityHelp: The name on their paperwork, and what they are to us.
company.tradeNameHint: If they are known by something shorter. Saved as an alias so search finds it.
company.rolesHint: A company can be both a client and a supplier. The first one chosen sets the code.
company.legalIdentityHelp: Décret 05-468 requires the client's NIF on an invoice, alongside our own RC, NIF, NIS and article d'imposition. Leave them empty now if you do not have them — the invoice will say what is missing when the time comes.
company.docLocaleHelp: Documents and email follow the COMPANY, not the person writing. Set French here and this client receives French paperwork even when an English-speaking colleague produces it.
company.aliasHelp: Every spelling anyone has used. Search matches all of them, and a merge adds the retired company's names here.
company.noContacts: Nobody recorded at this company yet.

bin.title: Deleted
bin.subtitle: Restorable for 30 days. After that the record is gone but its audit trail is not.
bin.emptyBody: Anything you remove lands here first, with who removed it and why.
bin.reasonPlaceholder: Why is it going? This is kept.
bin.removingHelp: Discard puts it in the bin for 30 days — for a record that should never have existed. Archive keeps it and every document that points at it, but takes it out of lists and search — for a client you no longer work with. An issued document is never deleted by either: it is cancelled, and an avoir keeps the number.
bin.blockedByIssued: This company has issued documents, so it cannot be discarded — a sent invoice must keep resolving. Archive it instead: it leaves the lists and every document still works.
bin.goneBody: Removed on {date}. You have {days} days to bring it back.
bin.afterThirtyDays: After 30 days the record is removed but the audit entry stays. In two years you can still find out that it existed and why it went.

empty.noCompaniesBody: Companies arrive when you add one, or when an email from a new sender is filed against a new record.
empty.noDealsBody: Deals appear here when you create one, or when an email in the Inbox is turned into one.
empty.errorBody: The server did not respond. Nothing was changed.
empty.noPermissionTitle: You do not have access to cost and margin
empty.noPermissionBody: The rest of this offer is visible. Ask the Gérant for {permission}.

invoice.companyIdentityIncomplete: Company identity is incomplete — RC, NIF, NIS or article d'imposition
invoice.vatServicesAbroad: VAT on services rendered abroad not confirmed

rules.unconfirmed: This rule has not been confirmed yet. It warns rather than blocks.
rules.comingInPhase: Not built yet — this arrives in phase {phase}.

merge.title: Merge duplicates
merge.subtitle: Two records, one company · you choose field by field, and nothing is lost
merge.duplicatesSubtitle: Two records that look like one company. Suggested, never automatic.
merge.noneBody: No two companies share a registration number, a tax number, an email domain, or a name close enough to flag. Pairs you have dismissed are not suggested again.
merge.leftIsKept: the left one is kept, and it keeps its reference

note.aliases: Both lists are kept — aliases are never a choice, they are added together. The retired code and name join them, so the old reference stays searchable.
note.nif: Fifteen digits. Often only one of the two records has them.
note.rcIdentical: Identical — this is why the system flagged them.
note.email: The other one becomes a contact rather than being thrown away.
note.paymentTerms: The newer record is proposed — it came off the last signed contract.

merge.nothingDropped: nothing is dropped, nothing is duplicated
merge.nothingAttached: Nothing is attached to either record yet. Documents, contacts and files appear here as they arrive.
merge.auditNote: Audit entries are not moved either — both trails are kept, and the merge itself is written into them: who, when, and every field chosen.

signalYes.similarName: after accents and spacing are stripped

merge.suggestedBody: Two companies can share a phone number and be genuinely different. The system proposes; a person decides. Not a duplicate is remembered, so the same pair is never suggested again.
merge.notADeleteTitle: A merge is not a delete
merge.notADeleteBody: {code} is retired, not removed. Every document that was ever issued under it keeps its number and still resolves. Nobody has to explain a missing reference to a client two years from now.

fourPlaces.contacts: the same person in two companies

merge.fourPlacesBody: One merge screen, four entities. Building it once is the difference between a tidy database and the Excel files this system replaces.
merge.banner: {count, plural, =1 {One pair of companies looks like the same client.} other {# pairs of companies look like the same client.}}

contacts.subtitle: {people} people at {companies} companies · {unverified} unverified · {bouncing, plural, =0 {no bouncing addresses} =1 {1 email bouncing} other {# emails bouncing}}
contacts.bouncingNeverReached: {count, plural, =1 {One email address is bouncing.} other {# email addresses are bouncing.}} {company} has never replied to a request — not because they are slow, but because nothing has ever reached them.
contacts.bouncingKnown: {count, plural, =1 {One email address is bouncing.} other {# email addresses are bouncing.}} Mail to {company} is coming back, so anything sent since is unread.
contacts.name: Name
contacts.jobHint: What they do at that company — Purchasing, Project manager, Legal.
contacts.prefersHint: How they answer fastest. Leave blank until you know.
contacts.emptyBody: A contact is a person at another company. Add the first one, or bring them in with the companies when the Excel move-in arrives.
contacts.whyOwnScreenTitle: Why this is its own screen
contacts.whyOwnScreenBody: A contact belongs to a company, but you deal with people. When a deadline is in six hours you search a name, not a company. And a person moves — the same buyer appears at a new employer and everything they told you should follow them.
contacts.newSubtitle: A name, a job, and the company they work for. The rest can wait.
contacts.newVerifyNote: A new contact starts as unverified — nobody has confirmed the address reaches them yet. It turns active the first time they reply.

error.jobRequired: Say what they do at that company — it is how you will find them later.
error.companyRequired: A contact belongs to a company. Choose one.
error.emailInvalid: That email address does not look right.
error.invalid: Something in the form was not accepted.

people.subtitle: {total, plural, =1 {1 person} other {# people}} · {fromCv} came from a CV, {rest} did not · a CV is evidence, not a requirement
people.directlyBanner: A person can be created directly — a name and a trade is enough. Day labourers, a subcontractor's welder, a driver hired for a week: none of them will ever send a CV, and all of them can be put on a project.
people.name: Name
people.tradePlaceholder: Soudeur, Électricien BT, Chef de chantier
people.emptyBody: A name and a trade is enough to start. The first person you add can be the driver you hired this morning.

origin.cv: A CV that arrived by any channel

people.whereFromBody: The candidate bank is one source of people, not the definition of one. A person exists in their own right; a CV, a certification and an ID copy are documents attached to them.

applies.project: Can be put on a project
applies.moyensHumains: Counts in moyens humains for a bid

error.tradeRequired: A trade is the second required field — Soudeur, Manœuvre, Chauffeur.
error.invalid: Something in the form was not accepted.

intake.channelsSubtitle: {total} ways work reaches SUPSERV · {live} are live · {losing, plural, =0 {none are losing records} =1 {1 is losing records today} other {# are losing records today}}
intake.losingRecords: The portal and paper channels have no path into the system. Anything arriving that way exists only in somebody's memory until it is typed in by hand.
intake.mailboxNotReading: The mailbox is not being read

channelAccepts.phone_note: A person writes down a call

intake.firstMatchWins: applied in order, first match wins

rule.cvFromStranger: Attachment is a CV and sender is not a known company
rule.rfq: Subject contains PR / RFQ / demande de cotation
rule.rfqAction: Enquiry, linked to the sender's company
rule.tender: Subject contains consultation / avis / appel d'offres
rule.supplierPrice: Sender is a known supplier and body contains a price
rule.supplierPriceAction: Supplier quote, attach to the open enquiry
rule.paymentAction: Payment, match against an open invoice

intake.sameAsAssistant: the same rules the assistant obeys

rail.neverAutoReply: Nothing is auto-replied to a client
rail.originalKept: Original email kept as the archive
rail.unmatchedToReview: Unmatched mail goes to Needs review

intake.railsNote: Enforced means there is no setting. Those three are constants in the code, because the moment one becomes a switch is the moment somebody turns it off at six in the evening to get a batch through.
